atoms.sound: True Crime Mini — Episode: The Murder of Martin Luther King Junior. I’ve got a wild one for you today. Ready? Picture this: it’s the evening of April 4th, 1968. Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. is chilling on the balcony of the Lorraine Motel in Memphis, Tennessee. He’s in town to back the striking workers. <voice voiceLang='en' voice='f3_2025'>Okay… I can already feel something bad’s about to happen.</voice> Then—bang. A shot rings out, King drops. Hours later, he’s gone: The man who shook the world with his words is taken out with a single rifle shot.  <voice voiceLang='en' voice='f3_2025'>Wow… that’s heavy. Who did it?</voice> James Earl Ray — a career criminal, already on the run. Weeks later, cops nab him in London. He confesses… and then takes it all back.<voice voiceLang='en' voice='f3_2025'> So, a straight-up “I did it… oh wait, no I didn’t”?</voice> Exactly. And that’s where the conspiracy theories start flying. Some say Ray was just a pawn in a much bigger game. Even now, the whole thing’s wrapped in mystery.<voice voiceLang='en' voice='f3_2025'>Which means?</voice> Which means one thing is crystal clear: that bullet didn’t just take a life. It shook an entire movement.
